## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).
data.title: Docs and demo notes

## Goal

Freeze the interfaces and pure logic for achievement-triggered game give-aways so the rest of the feature can be built and tested with no Steam, Electron, or real launcher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GiveawayRule` (target game id + required achievement ids) and `GiveawayRuleSet` are typed and documented in `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`; no game title is hard-coded in logic.
- Pure `evaluateGiveaways(unlockedAchievementIds, rules, alreadyUnlockedGameIds)` returns `{ gameId, unlocked, reason, missingAchievementIds }[]` with a discriminated `reason`.
- A unified multi-game `ContentUnlockStore` (memory + file implementation, corrupt-file-safe) generalises the existing single-game `UnlockStore`; the file store never throws.
- Unit tests cover: all required achievements met unlocks once; a subset blocks with `missingAchievementIds`; idempotent repeat; unknown/empty config is a no-op; a corrupt file degrades to empty state.
- Tests pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — types + pure evaluation.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` — share the persistence store as a multi-game store.
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-contract.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Contract module, unified multi-game unlock store, unit tests.
data.title: Give-away unlock contract and deterministic fakes (test-first)

data.description:
## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

# Core icon-linkage mechanism and scaffold tests

**Parent:** CG-0MUUFZSE90061KKL (Wire the app icon into each tce-<game> repo entry).

## Goal

Extend the scaffold's shared-asset linkage so the core's root app-icon files
compose into a scaffolded/refreshed game repo's `public/` root, giving every
`tce-<game>` a single-source-of-truth icon set.

## Scope

- Add `sharedPublicRoot` to `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` enumerating the
  six core root app-icon files: `favicon.svg`, `apple-touch-icon.png`,
  `icon-32.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `site.webmanifest`.
- Add exported `linkSharedPublicAssets(gameRepoRoot, coreRoot)` to
  `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, reusing the `linkSharedAssets()` symlink
  semantics (idempotent, relative targets, plain file symlink with a
  copy/junction fallback).
- Call it from `scaffoldGameRepo()` and surface the created links in the
  scaffold result.
- Keep `core/public/favicon.svg` the single source of truth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Core asset-linkage single source of truth: the scaffold's shared-asset linkage (`scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, driven by `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`) exposes the core root app-icon files (`favicon.svg`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, `icon-32.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `site.webmanifest`) into a scaffolded/refreshed game repo's `public/` root, derived from the tracked `core/public/` files — no hand-copied divergent icon binaries.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` declares the six root icon files in a `sharedPublicRoot` list.
- `scaffoldGameRepo()` invokes the new linkage and the returned result lists the created root icon links.
- Automated validation: `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` asserts the six root icon files are linked into a temp game repo's `public/` and that a second run is a no-op; the core unit suite (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass.
- Core changes committed and pushed to the core `dev` branch (never `main`), with the commit hash recorded on this work item.

## Definition of Done

- Mechanism implemented; the root-icon linkage is driven from `repo-layout.json` (no hard-coded file list in code).
- Tests written before/with the code and passing; build green.
- Pushed to core `dev`; commit hash recorded on the core work item.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — add the `sharedPublicRoot` list.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — add `linkSharedPublicAssets()` and wire it into `scaffoldGameRepo()`.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — new linkage tests.
- `public/favicon.svg` — authoritative source file (no change expected).
data.title: Core icon-linkage mechanism and scaffold tests

# Document base-relative icon-link convention

**Parent:** CG-0MUUFZSE90061KKL.

## Goal

Document how the core's app-icon set is shared into game repos and the
base-relative link convention, so future game repos follow it.

## Scope

- Add a section to `docs/DEVELOPER.md` covering the `sharedPublicRoot`
  linkage, `linkSharedPublicAssets()`, and the three icon links.
- Explain why hrefs are base-relative (no leading `/`, no `./`) so they
  resolve under the dev-server root, a GitHub Pages sub-path, and Electron
  `file://`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and any relevant docs under `docs/dev/`) documents the base-relative link convention and the icon linkage (`sharedPublicRoot` + `linkSharedPublicAssets()`); `public/assets/CREDITS.md` already records the emblem's provenance (no change expected); cross-repo pushes go to each game repo's `dev` only — never `main`.
- The doc states the three link tags and the six composed `public/` root files, and notes that `core/public/favicon.svg` is the single source of truth.
- Core unit suite and `npm run build` pass; the docs change is committed and pushed to core `dev`.

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria above are met and verified on the recorded commits.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — add the icon-linkage / base-relative convention section.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — the linkage being documented.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — the `sharedPublicRoot` data being documented.
data.title: Document base-relative icon-link convention

# Wire icons into tce-beleaguered-castle

**Parent:** CG-0MUUFZSE90061KKL.

## Goal

Give the standalone `tce-beleaguered-castle` app the core's tableau-emblem icon set, so a
standalone `npm run dev`/`npm run build` serves the correct
tab/bookmark/home-screen icons with no favicon 404.

## Scope

- Bump the `./core` submodule to the core `dev` tip containing the icon work
  (CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9).
- Add the three base-relative icon links to `index.html` immediately before
  `<title>`. The current generic title "Tableau Card Engine" is unchanged (making per-game titles is out of scope).
- Compose the six core root icon files into `public/` as committed symlinks
  back to `core/public/` (use `linkSharedPublicAssets()`, or create the
  equivalent manual symlinks matching the existing `public/assets/*` pattern).
  Do not re-run the full scaffold: it would clobber the game-specific
  `index.html`.
- Add a small unit test at `tests/game-icon-links.test.ts` asserting the three
  links are declared and each referenced `public/` file exists.
- Run `npm run test:unit` and `npm run build`; commit and push `dev` (never
  `main`). This repo has no Worklog store, so record the commit hash on this core work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every affected game entry declares the icon links: `tce-beleaguered-castle` `index.html` has base-relative `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="favicon.svg">`, `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="apple-touch-icon.png">`, and `<link rel="manifest" href="site.webmanifest">`, and every referenced file exists in `public/` and resolves in both `npm run dev` and `npm run build`.
- Submodule bump: the `tce-beleaguered-castle` `./core` submodule is pinned to a core commit that contains the icon work (CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9), i.e. the core `dev` tip or later.
- The `tce-beleaguered-castle` `public/` root contains the six core icon files (`favicon.svg`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, `icon-32.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `site.webmanifest`) as committed symlinks into `./core/public/` — no hand-copied divergent binaries.
- Automated validation: an automated test in `tce-beleaguered-castle` asserts the game entry declares the three icon links and that each referenced `public/` file exists; `npm run test:unit` and `npm run build` pass.
- Pushed to `tce-beleaguered-castle` `dev` only — never `main` — with the commit hash recorded on this work item.

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria above are met and verified on the recorded commits.

**Key Files:**

- `tce-beleaguered-castle/index.html` — add the three icon links before `<title>`.
- `tce-beleaguered-castle/public/favicon.svg` — committed symlink to `core/public/`.
- `tce-beleaguered-castle/public/site.webmanifest` — committed symlink to `core/public/`.
- `tce-beleaguered-castle/tests/game-icon-links.test.ts` — new link/file assertion.
- `tce-beleaguered-castle/.gitmodules` — verify the `core` pin with `git submodule status core`.
data.title: Wire icons into tce-beleaguered-castle

# Cross-repo icon wiring verification

**Parent:** CG-0MUUFZSE90061KKL.

## Goal

Independently verify, across all eight sibling game repos, that the icon wiring
landed correctly and record the evidence on the core work item.

## Scope

- For each affected repo: check `index.html` declares the three base-relative
  icon links; check every referenced `public/` icon file exists and resolves;
  check `./core` is at or after the icon commit.
- Run `npm run build` and the repo's test suite in each repo at the recorded
  commit.
- Record a coverage table (repo, `./core` pin, icon links present, public files
  present, test/build result, pushed commit hash) as a comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Cross-repo verification: every affected game repo's `index.html` declares the three base-relative icon links and each referenced `public/` icon file exists/resolves; every repo's `./core` pin is at or after the icon commit (CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9); and each touched repo's full test suite passes.
- Each of the eight repos passes `npm run build` and its test suite at the recorded commit.
- A coverage table (repo, `./core` pin, icon links present, public files present, test/build result, pushed commit hash) is recorded as a comment on this work item.
- Any repo that fails is linked to a follow-up work item; no repo is left silently unverified.

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria above are met and verified on the recorded commits.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — the linkage mechanism under verification.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — expected `sharedPublicRoot` list.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — the documented base-relative convention.
- `public/favicon.svg` — authoritative icon artefact.
